newsitem.title: SWEDEN: NCC sells NK Cityfastigheter for 64 Skr/share. [CORRECTED 10:41 GMT]
newsitem.headline: NCC sells NK Cityfastigheter for 64 Skr/share. [CORRECTED 10:41 GMT]

text.p: Swedish construction company NCC said on Friday it had sold the majority of its NK Fastigheter unit to institutional investors at home and abroad and to private Swedish buyers for 64 crowns a share.

The previously-announced offering was subscribed (corrects from "oversubscribed") eight times and the share would start trading on the Stockholm Stock Exchange's O list on March 21, the company said in a statement.
The price was at the top of the previously given range, 55-64 crowns a share.
NCC sold 12 million shares in NK Cityfastigheter, corresponding to almost 62 percent of the total number of shares, the company said.
The company might sell another 2.4 million shares, corresponding to more than 12 percent of the unit's total number of shares, if an over-allotment option is used.
Assuming full exercise of the over-allotment option, the sale will generate a capital gain of about 175 million crowns and a positive liquidity effect of about 1.1 billion crowns, the company said.

After the sale, and assuming the overallotment option is fully used, NCC will hold 5,060,666 shares, or 26 percent of NK Cityfastigheter's shares. The book value of the holding will be about 250 million crowns, the company said.
The group's equity-to-assets ratio will increase to nearly 30 percent from 28 percent.

"We are highly gratified at the substantial degree of oversubscription, which confirmed that the concept of niche-oriented real estate company is viewed favorably by the capital market," NCC's chief executive Jan Sjoqvist said.

"The company will have a strong circle of owners, with a significant element of international investors, which demonstrates that international interest in the Swedish real estate market is increasing."
